speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me your name and how old you are? Also, where exactly does it hurt when you walk?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain in your left knee wake you up at night, and does it hurt more when you run or play? Also, has your mother noticed if you are walking with a limp even when you aren't in pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain radiate from the knee down to your shin or up to your hip, and does it feel better when you rest or worse when you walk? Also, can you bend your left knee as far as your right one without pain?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain seem to come from your hip or groin area rather than just your knee, and do you have trouble turning your leg inward or lifting it up? REQUEST TEST: Pelvis_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray Left Hip findings indicate flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease. Vital signs are stable (Temp 36.8°C, BP 100/65 mmHg, HR 82 bpm, RR 18 breaths/min). Physical examination reveals tenderness on palpation of the left hip, pain with passive hip motion, and full range of motion in the knee with negative special tests for knee instability or meniscal tear.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms flattening of your femoral head, which points to a condition called Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease. This is why the pain feels like it's in your knee even though the issue is actually in your hip. DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease.
